walkthroughs.body_html:
Food Preparation Skills — a core area of GCSE Food Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Food Preparation Skills brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Food Preparation Skills.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many portions of fruit and veg a day are recommended?
Eatwell Guide is from which country?
options: USA
UK
Australia
Canada

mcqs.q: What are the 4 Cs of food hygiene?
options: Because they are illegal.
Cleaning, Cooking, Chilling, and avoiding Cross-contamination.
Calories, Carbs, Calcium, Cholesterol.
Chopping, Cleaning, Cooling, Carrying.

mcqs.q: On a traffic-light label, what does a red light indicate?
options: The food is organic.
High amounts of that nutrient per 100g - eat less often.
The food is dangerous and should never be eaten.
Calories, Carbs, Calcium, Cholesterol.

mcqs.q: Why must the 14 major allergens be highlighted on UK food labels?
options: Because they are illegal.
To advertise that the food contains them.
Reactions can be severe or life-threatening, so consumers must identify them at a glance.
The food is organic.

mcqs.q: Why are the 'bridge hold' and 'claw grip' taught when using a chef's knife?
options: They make food cook more quickly
They keep fingers tucked away from the blade to prevent cuts
They stop bacteria transferring to the food
They make vegetables taste better

mcqs.q: When making shortcrust pastry, why is the fat rubbed into the flour with the fingertips?
options: To develop long gluten strands for stretch
To melt the fat completely before baking
To coat the flour particles in fat, limiting gluten development and giving a crumbly texture
To add moisture so the pastry rises

mcqs.q: A student is making a roux-based white sauce. Why must the sauce be stirred continuously while it heats?
options: To add air so the sauce rises
To stop the starch granules sticking together in lumps and to help even gelatinisation
To cool the sauce down
To kill bacteria in the flour

mcqs.q: What is the most reliable way to check a grilled chicken breast is safely cooked?
options: Check that the outside is golden brown
Time it for exactly 10 minutes
Press it to see if it feels firm
Use a temperature probe to check the core has reached at least 75°C
